title: He Paddled Out of San Quentin
central_question: How did a bank robber escape San Quentin in a homemade kayak, and how did the man who said he escaped 18 times end?
content_notes: Respectful tone: remarkable and ironic, never glamorising. No weapon, threat, crash, injury or violence is depicted; no teller is shown in danger. Tucker (deceased) appears only as a faceless silhouette tagged NOT A LIKENESS; the two other 1979 escapers are faceless silhouettes and never named. Tellers, deputies, the tower guard, the trainer and the analyst are generic figures, never named; no badge, logo or name of any real bank, prison service or police force is drawn. The prison, bay, bank and road are generic illustrations. The escape count is attributed to him. No film imagery. Every card is our own typed graphic. No dialogue is invented. Status verified 2026-10-15.

lines.text: A bank robber paddled out of San Quentin.
He said he escaped 18 times.
How do you build a boat in prison?
He built it from plastic and duct tape.
He named it Rub-a-Dub-Dub.
Waves swamped it.
They still got away.
Twenty years later, at 78, he was still robbing banks.
And he sometimes thanked the tellers.
But police were already watching.
After a chase, deputies arrested him.
Ever caught in a bank robbery? Save these three rules.
30 percent of identified bank criminals were repeat offenders.
No kayak, this time.
The man who escaped 18 times died in prison, at 83.

claims.text: On 9 August 1979 Forrest Tucker, then 59 and serving a robbery sentence at San Quentin State Prison, California, escaped with two other inmates in a homemade kayak across the bay. Narration: 'A bank robber paddled out of San Quentin.'

REPORTED (his own count): Tucker said he had escaped 18 times (his manuscript outline asked whether anyone had escaped 18 times, Tampa Bay Times 1999; 'by his own reckoning ... 18 times successfully and 12 times unsuccessfully', per Wikipedia citing Grann). Grann's article: he broke out 'almost twenty times'. One lower-quality page says 16; the count is therefore attributed: 'He said he escaped 18 times', end card 'BY HIS COUNT'.
San Quentin State Prison is on San Francisco Bay, Marin County, California; the 1979 kayak was launched from a beach on prison grounds.
The kayak was built in the prison woodshop from plastic sheeting, wood, duct tape and Formica (Tucker built it while the two others kept watch, per Grann).
FUN FACT CARD: the boat was named 'Rub-a-Dub-Dub' (Tampa Bay Times: painted bright blue on one side with the words Rub-a-Dub-Dub in red; Grann: stencilled on the side).
Three men (Tucker and two other inmates, not named in the episode) paddled out from the prison shore.
Strong wind and waves swamped / capsized the kayak; the men still got away (the other two were recaptured later; Tucker stayed free for years).
On 22 April 1999, aged 78, Tucker robbed a bank in Pompano Beach, Florida, about twenty years after the kayak escape. Narration: 'Twenty years later, at 78, he was still robbing banks.'
Tucker was described by tellers as polite and a gentleman, and he sometimes thanked tellers after a robbery (he robbed at gunpoint; no weapon is shown or mentioned as a joke).
Police had him under surveillance even before the 22 April 1999 holdup.
After a car chase, sheriff's deputies arrested him (Tampa Bay Times: the chase ended when he crashed into a palm tree; the crash is not shown).

LESSON CARD (practical, respectful): police and bank-safety guidance for staff and customers during a robbery: stay calm and cooperate with the robber's commands; observe the robber's face and height; do not touch anything the robber touched, to preserve evidence. Rows: 'STAY CALM. DO AS TOLD.', 'NOTE THEIR FACE AND HEIGHT', 'TOUCH NOTHING THEY TOUCHED'.

STATISTIC (counter): of the 801 people identified among the 1,652 known to be involved in 2023 bank robberies, burglaries and larcenies at insured institutions, 30 percent had previous federal or state convictions for bank robbery, burglary or larceny (FBI Bank Crime Statistics 2023; the 2022 report gives 39 percent; Pinkerton's 2019-2023 analysis: about one third are repeat offenders). Narration: 'In 2023, 30 percent of identified bank criminals were repeat offenders.'
Tucker died in federal custody at the Federal Medical Center, Fort Worth, Texas, on 29 May 2004, aged 83. Narration: 'The man who escaped 18 times died in prison, at 83.'
